data.name: Sherlock Holmes - Nemesis
data.detailed_description:
Destaque


Acerca do jogo

Este novo jogo Sherlock Holmes remete-nos para a Londres do século XIX, no momento em que Arséne Lupin, um jovem ladrão francês com um registo de assaltos impressionante, lança um desafio à Scotland Yard e ao mais famoso dos detectives - Sherlock Holmes.

Esta nova aventura oferece aos jogadores uma tremenda liberdade e um ainda mais forte sentido de envolvência através dos gráficos 3D em tempo real. O jogo convida-o a visitar a Londres do século XIX em todo o seu esplendor e a percorrer os cenários soberbos, aqui reproduzidos de forma extremamente fiel.

Características

  • A magnífica cidade de Londres e todos os seus monumentos mais famosos (o Palácio de Buckingham, o Museu Britânico, a Galeria Nacional, a Torre de Londres...) são recriados de forma realista para os cenários da investigação.

  • Conheça a Rainha de Inglaterra numa audiência muito privada.

  • Interaja com mais de 40 personagens para aprofundar a sua investigação.

  • Vista a pele do famoso detective, Sherlock Holmes, e do seu fiel amigo, o Doutor Watson.

  • Use e combine mais de 100 objectos e descubra centenas de pistas e documentos para o ajudar a levar a investigação a bom porto.

reviews.review:
Abysmal direction and broken progression systems that turn a battle of wits into an infuriating guessing game.

If you are thinking of picking up Sherlock Holmes: Nemesis, it is a massive step backward for Frogwares that trades genuine detective work for contrived design choices. While chasing a flamboyant gentleman thief across massive historical London locations sounds like a brilliant premise, the actual game execution is an unoptimized chore that actively disrespects the player's time.

Here is what you need to know before diving in:

• Horrific Navigation and Map: The navigation system and map layout are aggressively broken. The game will routinely demand that you locate a specific shop or historical destination on a precise street, only for you to completely overshoot it because street names are entirely absent from both the map interface and the physical in-game environments. You will spend hours mindlessly circling back and retracing your steps through poorly optimized corridors just trying to figure out where the game wants you to go.

• Artificial, Mindless Backtracking: Progression relies entirely on exhausting colossal environments like the British Museum or the National Gallery by running back and forth to trigger arbitrary flags. Instead of using Sherlock’s intellect to piece together a case, you are subjected to agonizingly slow errands—like hunting down four literal birds in a massive courtyard or spending 20 minutes finding a single book on a sea of unmarked bookshelves just to fetch a tiny snippet of context.

• Pedantic, Strict Riddle Parsing: The text-input mechanics and word-association puzzles are brutally unpolished. When you are finally asked to answer questions and present your findings to Watson, the game's text parser demands hyper-specific, exact wording. If you do not type the exact, singular word the developers intended—even if your deductive logic is 100% sound and factual—the entire game stalls your momentum completely.

• Absurd, Contrived Tasks: The actual narrative substance quickly devolves from high-stakes mental warfare into a total farce. Rather than executing brilliant forensic analysis, the game forces the world's greatest detective to complete utterly ludicrous, immersion-breaking chores. You will find your patience pushed to its absolute limit as you spend your time preparing a specific meal for a dog or tracking down a collection of missing dolls inside Buckingham Palace.

Final Verdict: A structurally flawed puzzle hunt that replaces brilliant investigation with artificial friction. If you don't want to deal with unmapped streets, pedantic text boxes, and running in circles for hours, save yourself the headache and skip this entry entirely.
